rationale: mi50grad's measured TP=4 prefill is 32.12 tok/s vs TP=2 prefill 38.88 tok/s — TP-4 prefill regresses because PCIe AR payload scales linearly with L (5MB/layer at L=512 vs 10KB at L=1). flambeau's V2.32.a Mesh<4> Q4_1 prefill peaks at 566 tok/s L=8192 — already faster than mi50grad's TP-2 best on different model class. Switching prefill topology offers nothing; switching back to PP for prefill is the honest call.

i_reload_between_phases.description: After prefill, free PP weights, re-load with TP layout, then decode.
i_reload_between_phases.cost: PP load is ~14s on Qwen3.6-35B (project memory); doing this per-request is unacceptable. Per-session is acceptable but loses the prefill-decode-prefill chain pattern.

ii_tp_layout_for_prefill.description: Engage TP layout from load; prefill runs forward_prefill_pp on each rank's TP-sliced weights with world=1 effective (each rank does its slice; results aren't combined since prefill stays on one rank).
ii_tp_layout_for_prefill.cost: Per mi50grad and this rig's measurement: TP-4 prefill loses 30-40% throughput vs PP-4. Concretely on Qwen3.5-27B-Q4_1 at L=8192: 566 tok/s PP-4 → ~370 tok/s TP-4 (extrapolated).

iii_dual_storage_with_broadcast.description: Keep weights in TP-sliced layout; for prefill, peer-copy each rank's slices into a temp full-weight buffer for one-time use, run PP prefill on that, drop. Free temp after each prefill.
iii_dual_storage_with_broadcast.cost: Memory: full weight set transiently on each rank (~16 GiB extra per rank for 27B) — forbidden on 32 GiB MI50. PCIe broadcast is ~6.75 GB/s per peer (TP-0a cert) so 16 GiB across 3 peers = 7s of broadcast — re-amortised over the whole prefill if it's long enough but fatal for short prompts.

iv_tp_decode_only_keep_pp_prefill.description: TP topology owns decode; prefill stays on the existing PP path with PP-shaped weight loading. Two model loads at session start: PP weights for prefill + TP weights for decode. Total VRAM: ~2x base (worth it since 16 GiB Q4_1 + 16 GiB PP = 32 GiB total / 4 ranks = 8 GiB/rank PP + 4 GiB/rank TP = 12 GiB/rank — fits 16 GiB rank budget).
iv_tp_decode_only_keep_pp_prefill.cost: 2x weight VRAM per rank during the session. Acceptable for V2.32.a-class models on 32 GiB MI50; tight but workable. Long context (large KV) eats the rest.
iv_tp_decode_only_keep_pp_prefill.verdict: deferred to TP-5b-i2 — viable but needs measurement

v_tp_decode_only_no_prefill_in_tp_sessio.description: When --mesh-mode tp, bail prefill outright. User runs prefill via a separate PP session, hands off the post-prefill state to a TP decode session. KV cache transfer is the only cross-session payload (~hundreds of MiB at long context).
v_tp_decode_only_no_prefill_in_tp_sessio.cost: Two sessions. Operationally awkward but the cleanest separation. KV-transfer hop is dominated by HtoH copy (no peer-access between sessions).
v_tp_decode_only_no_prefill_in_tp_sessio.verdict: default for TP-5b — simplest correct shipping behaviour

v1_shipped: Option v: TP mode supports decode only. Prefill path errors out clearly with 'use --mesh-mode pp for prefill, switch to --mesh-mode tp for decode-only sessions'. The user runs prefill on PP, snapshots the KV cache, restarts with TP for the decode loop.
future_work: TP-5b-i2: implement Option iv (dual-storage) with measured per-rank-VRAM gates. Run on Qwen3-Coder-30B (smaller, fits 2× more comfortably) first.

Or TP-5b-i3: TP-aware prefill kernels (forward_full_attn_prefill_tp, forward_dense_ffn_prefill_tp, etc.) — biggest engineering lever but recovers full prefill perf without dual-storage. Multi-session work.
current_state: TP path remains structurally complete in code (TP-0..4 all shipped). Server engagement (TP-5a-i2) blocks first; this design only takes effect once the server actually engages TP at runtime.
